result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.

result.rule: When the description states that a participant performs a distinct action to initiate the process: Model a start event for the process trigger, followed by a task for the initiating action; do not use the start event to represent the action itself.

When the description states that the process begins when an incoming communication or request occurs, without describing separate work to receive it: Represent that occurrence with a suitable start event; model a separate receipt activity only when the description states that receiving it is work to be performed.

When the description says a later activity occurs after an earlier activity succeeds but does not describe an alternative outcome or failure handling: Model the stated sequence with a direct sequence flow; do not add a decision gateway solely to represent an unspecified failure path.

When When a description names multiple distinct activities within one phase and states that the process continues only after every activity is finished,: model the activities as parallel branches with a parallel split and join, rather than as a sequence.
